utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. First of all I would like to know whether that is what you -- what your evidence was you gave half a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As the editor of the Serbian Unity magazine, we had our photo department. I was editor-in-chief, and this could be inscription made by our technical editor. I was not duty-bound to mark the back of any of the photos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, apparently you are answering a question which I did not put to you. I tried to understand where you said: "I don't have that much time to write anything on the back of any of the photos," whether that was really your evidence. And I've asked you now twice or three times and apparently you are not inclined to answer my question. You may proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, what will be the lot of this photo? I would be satisfied with the admission of the photo alone without its back side. Has this been admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have shown the back of the photograph to the witness. And since I asked him questions about it, I think the photograph, as uploaded in e-court, that is, a three-page document, should be tendered. Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2D902 will receive number D664, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Pelevic, can we now look at one video-clip, 2D1011. While we're waiting for the booths to find the relevant transcript, tell me, Mr. Pelevic, when did Arkan return from the Banja Luka theatre of war with his unit?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in late October 1995, when the situation on the ground was finally stabilized.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 2D1011. This is part of the V000-7892. From 01 hour, 16 minutes, to 1 -- I apologise. 10 minute, 16 seconds, to 10 minute, 41 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Why are all the troops down there? Tell him to stop firing. What does this mean? Tell them not to shoot in the forest. Our men are there." [Zeljko Raznjatovic Arkan] [In English] "The special force of police and the Serbian Volunteer Guard were 800 metres from Kljuc, town of ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Pelevic, I have two questions for you. It seems that Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, himself says that they are near Kljuc. Do you recognise the person on the left-hand side next to Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was taken in the Banja Luka theatre of war. This is Ljubisa Borovcanin, who was either the commander or the deputy commander in charge of the special brigade of the Republika Srpska MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We saw your photo sporting a black beret and now we can see Arkan sporting a red beret. Can you tell us, What kind of berets did guard members wear during the war?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First we had green berets and then black berets. And then after the Vance Plan put a ban on the RSK army, we had blue berets. And finally we ended up with dark red berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now can we look at 1 minute, 41 seconds, to 2 minutes, 01 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Pelevic, first of all, can you tell us whether you know anything about this event depicted in the video-clip?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we just have a clarification of the time-code associated with this. I see on page 53, lines 2 and 3, there's a "1 minute, 41 seconds, to 2 minutes, 1 second," and I see the current video that's up on the screen is 2 minutes 15 seconds, just so we know what we watched.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. It should be 2.03 to 2.57. We could not stop the video-clip in the right place.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, could you please pay attention to the civilians and one person in a military uniform, and can you tell us whether you recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we play the tape again from 2.03 to 2.57.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Are you able to recognise people? We saw Arkan --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have seen now -- let's just assume that we started at 2.03, which is after we had seen the tank firing. And now for the second time it is stopping at 2.15, not on 2.57. Do you intend to play the remainder? Or is it that you want to put questions on these first 12 seconds? What is it, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to put a question about the initial first -- initial couple of seconds, and I would like to ask the witness whom he recognises in the video still, and then I would like to play the video-clip to the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So 2.57, we'll see that later. Please proceed. Ask the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Pelevic, we saw Arkan kissing an officer. And now at 2.15 seconds we see two civilians. Who are they?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person on the left-hand side is Tomislav Kovac, the minister of the police of Republika Srpska. And in the middle we can see Radovan Karadzic, the then-president of the Republika Srpska. On the right-hand side I recognise our general, Marko Pejic, a general in the Serb Volunteer Guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And you saw that Arkan was kissing an officer before that. Did you recognise that person?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was General Subotic, a general in the RSK. I don't know his first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we continue playing the video until the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this video-clip into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just -- Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just please have one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An MFI is what I'm requesting. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objection. Your Honour, I believe at this time there is some context missing in terms of what it is and things of that matter. But we're not objecting just for the purpose that the video was shown to him and he identified individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just checking, Mr. Bakrac, what you told us about -- after you put some questions to the witness about who he recognised, then we looked for 40 seconds at people walking amidst the crowd. What are we supposed to do with that? Is the crowd important? Is it -- what is it that you seek to establish by us looking for 40 seconds at the video?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do apologise. Perhaps I made a mistake. But our position is that it is important to see the relationship that Arkan had with the president of the republic, Karadzic, with the minister of police, Tomo Kovac, and with the representative of the army, the representative of the Army of Republika Srpska. Given previous testimony, I don't want to mention the name. That was my idea when I decided to show this for the benefit of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that for the first 15 seconds, but for the last 35 walking -- okay, let's -- it takes most likely more time to get it reduced, but could you please focus on what really is relevant. And is he establishing how many persons -- if you want us to look at the gentlemen walking amidst the crowd, then five seconds would really do, more than that. The problem is Madam Registrar has no copy of this video. How is she supposed to deal with it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I requested that it be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But even for it to be marked for identification, we need something in e-court. The matter seems not to be resolved by saying, "I only want it to be MFI'd," because we need something in the system to know what is MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll wait ... We'll wait until you have provided the Registry with such a copy that we could consider marking it for identification. Perhaps a number could be reserved for that purpose, even if we have no underlying document. But one number that will be reserved is ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Video 2D1011 will receive reserve number D665, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it's not yet marked for identification but the number is reserved for it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm looking at the clock, Your Honour, and please don't misunderstand me, I wanted to be precise prior to this session. I was told that my examination had taken up three hours and seven minutes. There were also certain preliminary issues that had to be dealt with. I think I have now used up about 55 minutes, perhaps. Could I have an additional half an hour, please? Because I have to conclude with this theme and then move on to one other subject. And Mr. Jordash has also said that he will need less time for his examination. So I would request that you allocate an additional half an hour for me, if possible, and we could then have the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, the three hours and seven minutes was at 11.00 after we had dealt with the preliminaries. So then you really started. You took 65 minutes since then. That makes four hours and 12 minutes. You're now asking for another half an hour, indicating that Mr. Jordash would take less time. Since we do not know how much time he had in his mind and how much time he says he needs now ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm happy to give up half an hour, I think, from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From one hour and a half? Was that the original ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Two hours was my original estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time would you need, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Four hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pelevic -- Mr. Pelevic, could I address you for a second. It looks that it may be possible that we would not conclude your testimony this week. I don't know whether travel plans you've made. I noticed from your answers that you're a very busy man. Is -- could you stay in The Hague until the beginning of next week to conclude your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as I was told, my testimony would take three days. And as I was told that it would be completed by the end of the week, I had certain plans. I have meetings scheduled at the university in Novi Sad and Belgrade for next week, but I will try to postpone the exams that were to be held, since about 100 students were expecting me. So if you so request, I will stay on in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Indiscernible] ... a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you at least consider that possibility. And would the parties further consider to see whether we could have an extended session perhaps tomorrow, tomorrow afternoon, so that if possible, with the assistance of everyone, that we could seek to conclude the testimony of this witness still this week. That should be our aim. But if you would consider, if we do not achieve that aim, if you would please consider the possibility of staying over the weekend. We take a break -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. Would it be -- with Your Honour's leave, could I have the witness look at four documents over the break? I think that would save a little bit of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that if you would inform the Prosecution about what documents they are and if they do not object, that there should be no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fine. Then, Mr. Bakrac, you get your half an hour. But if you could reduce it, then that would be highly appreciated. Perhaps reduce the time of parts of videos we're looking at. We resume at 20 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Our late start is due to technical matters to be resolved. Mr. Jordash, before we continue, could I ask you to give, soon, the position of the Stanisic Defence in terms of right to be present, use of videolink, if need be, or just a refusal, to say, "No, Mr. Stanisic wants to be in court. Even if we would have a second session tomorrow in the afternoon, he's unable to come, so therefore ..." You see, your position in view of all the possible solutions for concluding the evidence of this witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think I can give that now. Mr. Stanisic is -- is going to, at some point, receive the second dose of the new medicine. Aside from that, he will be present if there's extended sitting hours. If he receives that during the time Your Honours want to sit, he's happy for proceedings to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So tomorrow afternoon would not --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- be a problem for the Stanisic Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then there may be all kind of other problems, but I thought it wise to first inquire with you, because that's a -- I would say, if there would be a problem, it would be a fundamental issue, rather than a practical issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then, Mr. Bakrac, are you ready? Half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Pelevic, let's now have a look at a video-clip. It's a DVD that we received from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From 1 minute, 46, up until 2 minutes and 15 seconds, Your Honours. 2D1016 is the number. 2D1016.2. There is no sound, Your Honour. The first part at least has no sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Pelevic, there's some military vehicles and some soldiers that can be seen here. Can you tell us on which occasion this video was made; and who are these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a celebration of the anniversary of the SDG. The date is the 10th of October, 1990 -- 1995 in Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We also saw some vehicles. What kind of vehicles are they and who do they belong to? Or who did you belong to then on the 10th of October, 1995?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We belonged to the Army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. And these are our vehicles that we received from the Army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we please now have a look at the next clip from the very same DVD. 8:52 to 9:28 seconds is the extract we're interested in.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Serbian volunteers and officers, it is my honour and duty to greet you in the name of the Serbian Volunteer Guard and in the name of its commander, Zeljko Raznjatovic Arkan. As you can see, he could not be here with us today because he is on the front line in the Banja Luka Krajina."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise. It's not 9:28, but 9:22. 9:22; 9 minutes and 22 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Pelevic, is this a speech from that very same anniversary celebration?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that Commander Arkan was in the Banja Luka Krajina. You said that the date was the 10th of October, 1995. Tell me, when did you go there? You said you visited the area for five or -- four or five days. When did you go to visit the Banja Luka Krajina?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact date, but I remember it was several days after.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see the following extract: 16 minutes and 20 seconds is where I would like us to start. This is an extract from the same DVD.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please tell us - it's 16 minutes and 20 seconds; we have frozen the image - who is the individual to the left? We can see two individuals. Who is the person to the left and who is the person to the right?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the left you can see General Marko Pejic, Peja, from the SDG wearing a red beret; and to the right, with a blue beret, you can see General Obrad Stevanovic, the commander of the PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say the PJP unit, which one?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a unit from the Serbia MUP. The MUP in Serbia, after the fall of the western part, or, rather, of the Knin Krajina in the western part of Republika Srpska, after that fall, they were sent to the border of the Republic of Serbian Krajina and to the Republic of Serbia because an attack on Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem was expected.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Pelevic, let me just see -- let us just have a look at another short extract of the DVD. 16:46 to 17:09 seconds is the part we are interested in.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "All convicts of the Serbian Volunteer Guard have been amnestied. In the name of the Serbian Volunteer Guard, I call on you to join us in this modest army lunch. Thank you for coming today to give dignity to our commemoration, because this is not a celebration - this is not the time for celebrations. This is a troop review of a battalion of the Serbian Volunteer Guard and a commemoration for our dead."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Pelevic, in this part you said that all of the convicts of the Serbian Volunteer Guard had been amnestied. What is at stake, in fact?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was common practice in the SDG on the day of the anniversary of the Serbian DG, the 10th of October, it was the practice to amnesty the convicts from the SDG. Not all of them, but most of them. Those who had shown remorse, who had demonstrated that they wouldn't act as they had acted. And that was common practice in the SDG. Unfortunately, I was replacing the commander who was in the Banja Luka battle-field that year and I amnestied all the convicts of the Serbian Volunteer Guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could 2D1016.2 please be given an MFI number. I do apologise. Could we first see 18:35 first of all. 18 minutes and 35 seconds. It's just a matter of identifying an individual. It's important for me to do this. 18:35.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Pelevic, can you tell us who this individual wearing a beard is? The individual we can see on the DVD at 18 minutes and 35 seconds.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the team director from Belgrade whose name is Mika Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you receive from Mika Aleksic certain materials after the war?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did receive certain videos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If Mr. Bakrac could please ask the questions from here on out in an open-ended fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No leading questions is what Mr. Weber is asking you, Mr. -- from now on. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. I do agree. It's just because of time restrictions. It wasn't ill-intentioned. Could this DVD please be given an MFI number, Your Honour. 2D1016.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 2D1016.2 will receive number D666, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Pelevic, let's please have a look at 2D527 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2D527. Can this be zoomed in, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Here we have an unsigned document. This is a certificate issued for Tomislav Drazovic. Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is one of the many regular documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you have provided Tomislav Drazovic's file, which included the certificate together with some other documents?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it true that on the 15th of November, 1995, you were indeed in Erdut, military post 819-09?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it true that Major Mladen Sarac at the time was the Chief of Staff of the Serbian Volunteer Guard?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to tender 2D527. It is linked to 2D529, personal file for Tomislav Drazenovic [as interpreted], son of Aleksandar. And the document was already shown to the witness. Can this be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution requests that it be marked for identification subject to cross-examination. We'd also ask that we be provided with the complete file, if it's been provided to the Simatovic Defence, before tomorrow so we could prepare for it, for cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will provided all the personal files, including the certificates. Let me just check something with my Case Manager. Your Honour, we received these documents earlier, and they have been on our 65 ter list since June. We received them before June from Mr. Pelevic. And since June they have been included in our 65 ter list. There are another three or four, perhaps even five, personal files that have all been disclosed to the Prosecutor already. They were disclosed sometime in June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would that be the complete files from which these documents are taken?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is what we received from Mr. Pelevic, and it was explained to us at the time that several personnel files were found on him. I have their originals which I can show Mr. Weber instead of the scanned copies. The originals contain coloured photographs and original stamps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, would you be interested to have a look at the originals and then perhaps at the same time have an opportunity to look at what is there in terms of complete files or more documents, same personnel files?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that would be acceptable to the Prosecution. We would request that the Simatovic Defence try to make contact with us to show those files today, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I would say from both sides you will see contact and you will meet each other somewhere. Then it would be marked for identification, this document. Madam Registrar that would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2D527 will receive number D667, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Pelevic, Mr. Pelevic, I have to put another three questions very quickly to you to bring this topic to an end. After the -- the events in Banja Luka and after the mission in Banja Luka Krajina, did SDG receive recognition from Republika Srpska? And if that was the case, who was the recognition from?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SDG, after the events in Banja Luka Krajina, received a thank-you note which was signed by the president of Republika Srpska, Dr. Radovan Karadzic. Also, Commander Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, received another thank-you note on the same occasion also from Radovan Karadzic, the president of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can we now look at 2D1019. And while we are waiting for the document to be displayed: Mr. Pelevic, where is this thank-you note physically at the moment?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both thank-you notes are in my house. In the memorial room of the SDG that I myself founded.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it true that you took photos of the thank-you notes, and did you send the photos to our Defence team?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is this the thank-you note that was bestowed on the SDG by Dr. Radovan Karadzic on the 22nd of October, 1995?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can 2D1019 be admitted into evidence. And I would like to say that the date on the second note of appreciation is not clearly visible. If Mr. Weber has any objection to its admission, it can be MFI'd, pending a better copy that may be provided. I'm talking about document 2D1018. The date on 21019 [as interpreted] is visible. Or perhaps we could try and look at 2D1018 in e-court. They tell me that the image is better in e-court. I believe that we can see it now. If Mr. Weber has no objections to the document's admission, I would like to tender both documents into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objection to 2D1019. The only difference that the Prosecution can observe from 2D1018, aside from the name, is the signature of Dr. Karadzic is not visible, but we can see the date. With that being noted, no objection to that either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the one, the -- apparently the signature is either fading or is difficult to see. But since there are no objections, we'll keep this in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2D1019 will receive number D668, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And finally, did Mr. Raznjatovic get a decoration from the president of Republika Srpska? And if that was the case, when did that transpire?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The following year, 1996, Commander Arkan was decorated by the highest decoration of Republika Srpska and the Serbian people in general. He received the Medal of Karadjordje's Star by Radovan Karadzic. I was decorated with a medal for [indiscernible], Milos Obilic, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we look at 2D1042, which I would like to tender for admission. This is also something we received from this witness. Your Honour, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2D1042 will receive number D669, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to broach my last topic just briefly, and I would like to bring my examination-in-chief to an end.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Pelevic, where were your offices in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our offices in Belgrade were in Ljutice Bogdana Street, number 3, across the street from the Red Star stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was that also the headquarters of the Serbian Unity Party?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the day of its foundation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you and Mr. Arkan have a personal assistant or a secretary?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The two of us had separate offices on the first floor. They were next to each other. And in the hallway in front of our two offices there was our secretary's desk.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can we move briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Jordash, are you ready? Mr. Pelevic, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Jordash. Mr. Jordash is counsel for Mr. Stanisic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I want to ask you about some of the evidence you've given and just to seek some further details and some clarifications, if I may. First of all, the subject I want to discuss with you is your evidence about the animosity between the Tigers and the Serbian DB and how Radovan Stojicic fits into that picture. You appear to be making a distinction between the personal relation that Badza had with Arkan and the relationship that Arkan had with the Serbian MUP as an institution. Did I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you have understood me correctly. He was happy about the relationship between the two co-fighters and two friends, and this continued to be the case up until Badza's death. This has nothing to do with the relationship between the SDG and the Serbian MUP or state security.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You spoke yesterday about the agreement between Arkan and the minister of defence of Serbia which allowed Arkan's Men, your group, to cross the border, and that was done in order to avoid police checks. Which time-period are you -- or were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the case throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was there a time when the police checks were particularly obstructive to the activities of the Tigers?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of those checks, we decided that no one could go from Belgrade to Erdut in uniform or in the other direction, and that included going there with weapons. So we -- in that manner, we managed to avoid having our members being checked by the Serbian MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You testified yesterday to using military routes because all the other crossings were closed by the police controls. Could you describe a bit more what you meant by "military routes"?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's, Your Honours, page 16373.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was war, and naturally, when you have any extraordinary situations in any country the army takes over command; and, thus, the army was in a position to create its military routes that were independent of these police check-points. And we used these routes when we went to the western part of the Republic of Serbian Krajina and to Republika Srpska from Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But when you described "military routes," are you describing different roads, different places to cross the border, and so on? What precisely are you describing? And how was it that this avoided police control?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since we mainly used military trucks for transport, and a while ago I said that the army was in control, it was the highest authority in such extraordinary circumstances, since that was the case, we used improvised routes. They weren't asphalted routes. They were improvised. Naturally, in peacetime there are no such routes, because they passed through police check-points controlled by the police. But at the time of the war there were such routes which we used.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have on the screen, please, D206, and it's not to be shown to the public. It's confidential.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Just for your information, Mr. Pelevic, there is -- what you're going to see is a report by the State Security Centre dated June of 1992, and this may answer one of your long-standing questions about an agent working in the Serbian Volunteer Guard. If you'd just read the first few lines. Just ensure you understand what this is. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And it brought a smile to my face.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's go over to the next page. The bit I'm interested in, for the moment, is the last paragraph, which deals with the police discovering and confiscating a large consignment sent to the SDG but then Arkan relying upon his personal relationship with Badza to get the matter resolved. Is that consistent with what you observed concerning the relationship between the Serbian MUP, the SDG, and Arkan and Badza?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, the first paragraph I read through, as you suggested, is really funny. Laughable. I can't command on it. Because to throw over the government in Belgrade and bring back the Karadjordjevo Dynasty, well, that's just laughable, especially since it was agreed with --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm short of time. I do apologise. I don't mean to be rude. I'm interested in whether this last paragraph, the Serbian MUP stopping the consignments to the SDG, was within your experience; and, secondly, was it within your experience that Arkan would, instead, rely upon his personal relationship with Badza to resolve such difficulties?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I have seen the document. But the last paragraph is something that is quite possible. I don't know what this event is. But it's quite possible that Arkan called Badza, his friend, to resolve the problem. But, as I said, I don't really know what it is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. In terms of the agent, you testified about the -- the -- a man being suspected of being an agent and then being thrown out of the SDG. Presumably there was a huge amount of conversation about this, as you spoke to Arkan about the fact that the Serbian DB may well have infiltrated the Tigers and were seeking to damage the organisation. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Your document has helped me to make sure that my conscience is clear. We didn't expel him from the guards for no reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And how concerned was Arkan about the Serbian DB and what the Serbian DB were seeking to do in relation to Arkan's Tigers? I'm talking about 1992 particularly, at this moment.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously the DB tried to obstruct the SDG from the very time it was founded, but the DB didn't have the strength or the manpower to prevent the SDG from operating militarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You say: "Obviously the DB tried to obstruct the SDG." Well, it may be obvious to you, but can you testify why you say that; what you observed to reach that conclusion? I'm not disagreeing with you. I'm just asking you to elaborate on why you came to that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I will be concrete. It's difficult to speak about this war-time period, but I'll provide you with an example of the elections in Serbian in 1993. The head of the campaign of Slobodan Milosevic's party, I won't provide you with the name, told us that since he was a friend of mine he told me and Arkan that our votes had been stolen at the elections, and he said that this had been done by the DB through certain politicians in Serbia who kept placing obstacles in our path and enter parliament before us. I believe this gentleman. But you can't be given a document, I can't provide you with a document, because, as you know, the secret service has no such documents. But that is the truth.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander Arkan told me several times to pay close attention to the person you have just mentioned. However, I did not share his opinion that she might be a DB spy. Simply, that person just did not have such a capacity as to work for DB, nor was she able to assist the DB from her position or to disclose any important military or political intelligence to the DB. So I thought that she was so harmless that there was really no need to check on her.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But, certainly, Arkan spoke to you on several occasions about the fact that he didn't trust her, and the reason he didn't trust her was because he thought she, too, was connected to the DB. That's the situation?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've just told you that. However, I did not take any of that seriously.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The same witness, P1615 [sic], said that Arkan was concerned to -- was concerned about the DB because he felt that the DB was observing and trying to stop his smuggling operation. Are you able to testify to that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PELEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The DB, I'm sure, followed Arkan and possibly me. As for a smuggling operation, I don't know what you mean. What that person meant is war-time, the time when you smuggle things? No. There was no such thing going on in our midst. As for sending packages in order to avoid the DB or the Serbian MUP control, if that's what you mean, then the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could you just elaborate on that. Apart from these military routes that were taken to avoid the Serbian MUP, can you think now what else was done, in terms of these packages you've just mentioned, to avoid the Serbian DB?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, before we start a whole new series, because this might be the beginning, I'd like -- to start with, I would like to know: Packages with what in it? That's the first question, I think, but that might be the last question for today as well. What was in those packages you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I did not mention any packages. I said dispatches of all kinds ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What kind of dispatches? Relating to what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I said is -- there were consignments of any sort. We tried to bypass and avoid the control of the Serbian MUP and DB. For example, we had to transport uniforms from Novi Sad and from a factory in Kosovo to Erdut. We had to do that, bypassing the police control because they would have confiscated those, I'm sure. That's what I meant. I didn't mean weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No one talked about weapons at this moment. So it's -- it's -- the question arises why you relate the question to weapons. It was, I think, just that smuggling operations, smuggling things, which -- so apparently you understood to be related to weapons, but you've now clarified that what you do know is about, as an example, uniforms. We adjourn for the day. We'll work out a schedule for tomorrow. We'll see whether we can sit for such times that we could conclude your evidence tomorrow. We'll try to do our utmost best, Mr. Pelevic. I again instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, whether given yesterday or today or whether still to be given tomorrow. What I also would like to invite the parties to do is to try to work out a schedule, leaving some time for questions by the Judges, and then to see whether you could agree on the time you would still need. Of course, I know that it's -- sometimes it's difficult to forecast how much time you would need, but if you make a schedule, then, of course, unexpected circumstances may have an influence on such a schedule. We need to know, because scheduling -- some of the Judges have also commitments tomorrow in the afternoon, so we have to try to get everything together. So close co-operation with Chamber's staff and with the Registry is required up to a high level of detail. We -- Yes, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise, I had to ask you to bear with me just for a minute. I would like to talk about our schedule, rather, about the witness that we asked to come on the 27, on Saturday, that's DFS-017. He was provided with safe conduct for December, but his appearance was rescheduled. My colleague has applied for the safe conduct application to be renewed for this witness. I hope we may resolve this situation before Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, I don't know whether you missed the filing of yesterday in which the safe conduct, that a new notice was sent, which was available to you as well. I said that the Chamber would take action, and that's what we did yesterday. So no need to revisit the matter today. I would say check at what was filed yesterday. Unless you have reviewed that and there's any problem with that, then we'd like to hear from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. My colleague Mr. Petrovic is not with me today. He is the one who has been dealing with that. I just wanted to avoid any possibility of us not having a witness next week. That's why I've mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's appreciated. We adjourn. And resume tomorrow, 9.00, on Thursday, the 26th of January, in this same courtroom, II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 26th day of January, 2012, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25
